messages:
sam: dropping an alternate approach for the latency dashboard 1 - single compact card that toggles between heatmap and p95-over-time with a small inline sampling control. want quick UX + a11y takes before I finalize the prototype. figma: https://figma.com/file/alt1

marta: nice. two quick asks: 1) show current bin size somewhere obvious (users ask this a lot), 2) the compact card needs a clear affordance for switching views (heatmap <-> timeseries).

ken: +1 for bin indicator. for the view switcher, could we do segmented control with icons and a short-label tooltip? keeps it tight. also: when switching to timeseries, animate height so user understands it's the same data.

liz: microcopy nit: instead of "sampling" label use "Capture rate" and add inline helper: "affects fidelity & cost". also add a tiny "why this matters" link that opens docs.

oliver: UX question: when capture rate is low, p95 may look unstable. can we show a confidence cue (e.g., faded error band or a small "low sample" badge) when sample count < threshold?

sam: yes, plan is to show a subtle diagonal hatch overlay on cells with low sample counts and a tooltip: "low sample: results may be noisy".

tasha: accessibility: hatch + color alone isn't great. add explicit textual indicator for screen readers like aria-describedby on the card summary. Also ensure the segmented control has aria-pressed and keyboard focus states.

a11y-bot: checklist: 1) segmented control must be reachable with keyboard; 2) state changes announced (aria-live region or aria-atomic summary); 3) heatmap cells must expose time, bin-size, percentile value via aria-label; 4) low-sample badge should be textually readable (not just icon).

ken: perf note: compact card will be reused many places; virtualize cell rendering and pre-aggregate server-side for large windows. client-side masks for legend toggles to avoid refetch storms.

infra-bot: reminder: backend limit on heatmap cells per request = 20k. recommend adding server-side aggregation for >= 10k cells.

oliver: design idea: when user hovers p95 datapoint show a small microband representing p90-p99 and a diff indicator vs previous period (+/- ms). helps triage regressions quickly.

marta: love that. keep the microband subtle, and in compact mode collapse it into the tooltip to avoid clutter.

liz: copy suggestion for the hover diff: "+12 ms vs prev period (p95)". for small diffs show "+12 ms" in green if negative? wait, green = better, so "-12 ms" should be green. we'll need color rules consistent with a11y.

tasha: color rules: don't rely on color alone for increase/decrease. add +/- sign and consider triangle icon up/down. also ensure contrast of the diff chip >= 4.5:1 when used as standalone text.

sam: keyboard flow proposal: Tab to card -> segmented control -> capture rate input (preset + stepper) -> view switch -> heatmap grid (arrow navigation cell-to-cell with roving tabindex) -> metrics action menu. Esc should exit any focus traps.

ken: arrow navigation for heatmap seems complex if we have many cells. suggest roving focus that jumps by visible columns/rows and a quick-jump shortcut (press G to jump to focused metric) for power users.

oliver: interactions: clicking a cell should open a small detail flyout with raw sample count, p50/p90/p95/p99 and example query snippet. provide a copy-to-clipboard button.

a11y-bot: flyout accessibility: focus trap if modal, restore focus on close, provide descriptive heading, and ensure flyout content is reachable by screen readers. copy button must announce success.

liz: analytics names to include in handoff: `latency.card.view_switch`, `latency.capture.update`, `latency.cell.open_details`. provide example payloads: { "view":"heatmap", "bin":"5m" }.

marta: final design ask: small persistence rules: remember last view per user (heatmap vs timeseries) and remember capture rate per org but allow quick override per page.

sam: noted. i'll bake those into the prototype and the Figma spec. planning to hand off assets + accessibility spec by EOD Friday. thanks for the fast feedback :sparkles:
